probes.prompt: /cwc-makers:m5-onboard Two provisioning requests arrive in one session at the makers booth; apply the skill decision rules to each and record the outcome in m5-onboard-plan.md. Headless boundary: no device is plugged in, no USB access, no network, no real external service and no installs; the plan documents what would run on the booth workstation, so detection, firmware download, flashing and app installation remain untested. Request A: the visitor plugs in their Cardputer-Adv and says same thing as last time; apply the documented repeat-visitor rule so the plan defaults to --apps buddy, record the default variant --variant cardputer-adv, and record the documented Bash-tool launch pattern for the full fresh run: the skill forbids running onboard.py as a foreground Bash command, so launch with run_in_background: true using the tee pattern python3 scripts/onboard.py --apps buddy 2>&1 | tee /tmp/m5-onboard.log and monitor with tail -f /tmp/m5-onboard.log. The plan must note this is a native-USB ESP32-S3 target so the flash stage runs at 115200 with --no-stub, and it must not mention the forbidden 921600 rate anywhere. When the monitored log shows Enter download mode, the plan must relay the required coaching and stop: press and HOLD BtnG0, briefly press BtnRST, release BtnRST first, keep holding BtnG0 for ~1 more second, release BtnG0, screen should be fully dark; the flash waits until the user confirms the screen is dark. Request B: a second visitor now says their board is a Cardputer with no Adv in the name; apply the variant rule: the plan must ask which model before flashing, must cite that flashing the wrong one boot-loops the device, and must record no provisioning command for Request B until the user answers. Then read the immutable verify_onboard_plan.py and run exactly python verify_onboard_plan.py using Bash; it validates the plan and writes onboard-verification.json.
